capitals.name: Sarai (Old Sarai, Selitrennoye; later New Sarai)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Sarai (western wing, later overall); Sighnaq (eastern wing)', no dates. The pages opened do not date the move from Old to New Sarai; coordinates are the gazetteer's Old Sarai (New Sarai is at 45.35 E, 48.68 N). The Great Horde page: Sarai sacked 10 June 1502.

rulers.name: Toqta (Tokhta)
rulers.note: Replaced Talabuga in 1291; died 1312 'crossing the Volga'.

rulers.name: Oz Beg (Ozbeg)
rulers.note: The page gives both 'assumed the throne in 1313' and 'reign 1312-1341'.

rulers.name: Berdi Beg (Berdibek)
rulers.note: Killed in a coup by his brother Qulpa in August 1359; the khans of 1359-1380 are listed in the Mamai page and are not repeated here.

rulers.name: Tokhtamysh
rulers.note: Golden Horde infobox 1379-1395; the Tokhtamysh page has him take Sarai in early 1380. The khans of 1396-1434 (Timur-Qutlugh, Shadi Beg, Edigu's puppets, Ulugh Muhammad) are not given with reign years on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Ahmed Khan bin Kucuk
rulers.note: Killed by Ibak of Sibir on 6 January 1481.

rulers.name: Sheikh Ahmed
rulers.note: Co-ruler with Murtaza Khan 1481-1498 (sole khan 1498-1499) per the page list; the infobox gives Sheikh Ahmed 1481-1502, the text 1499-1502.

keyframe_review.note: 4.93 M km2 for 1294-1304; the infobox gives 6.0 M km2 'in 1310' (ratio 0.82 against the 1305 shape, within the factor of two). The gazetteer puts the whole Kiev core, Podolia and Moldavia inside the shape, which the Battle of Blue Waters page supports until 1362 ('Kiev ... still paid tribute to the Horde' after the early-1320s Irpin River battle). The Rus' princedoms (Vladimir-Suzdal, Moscow) are separate Cliopatria rows and enter as vassal tint through the ledger. The frontier is a steppe frontier: soft. fx-13 (F308): 156 cells of modern Georgia (Abkhazia, Samegrelo, Imereti, Racha, Shida Kartli, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, Guria, Kakheti, Samtskhe-Javakheti) lie in this outline. The Golden Horde page has the Horde 'bordering the Caucasus Mountains and the territories of the Mongol dynasty known as the Ilkhanate', says of Tode Mongke (from 1281) that he 'might have had an interest in Azerbaijan and Georgia, which were both ruled by the Ilkhans', and has Berke 'marched past Tiflis' in 1264 as a campaign, not a holding; the Tokhtamysh page has a raid 'across the Caucasus into Shirvan' (1394) and no raid on Georgia. Georgia is cut out; the Terek-Caucasus frontier stays.

keyframe_review.note: 4.42 M km2 for 1385-1394. Reunited realm: Tokhtamysh 'the first khan in over two decades to rule both halves'; 1383 Khwarazm restored; winter 1384-85 Tabriz stormed (the shape's bbox reaches 37.8 N, south of Tabriz). Two adjustments: (1) Cliopatria leaves Crimea (0 of 106 cells) out of the Golden Horde and draws it as the Blue Horde until 1449; the pages have Crimea within the Horde's sphere (Tokhtamysh made peace with the Genoese of Crimea in early 1381), so it is added back; (2) Timur razed Gurganj in 1388, so Khwarazm (647 of 844 cells in the shape) was at best contested from 1388 (ledger). fx-13 (F310): 137 cells of Iran (East Azarbaijan 68, Ardebil 66, 3 more) are cut out. Tokhtamysh page: 'He captured the capital, Tabriz, by storm and ravaged the neighboring area for ten days', then no annexation ('Timur proceeded to conquer Azerbaijan in 1386'); Jalayirid Sultanate page: 'Tabriz was briefly looted by the Golden Horde in 1385' and the sultanate keeps Tabriz until Timur takes it in 1386. A storming and a looting are not a holding, so the Horde draws no Iranian land in 1385-1394. (F308) 2 cells of modern Georgia (Svaneti, in Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti) lie in this outline. The Golden Horde page has the Horde 'bordering the Caucasus Mountains and the territories of the Mongol dynasty known as the Ilkhanate', says of Tode Mongke (from 1281) that he 'might have had an interest in Azerbaijan and Georgia, which were both ruled by the Ilkhans', and has Berke 'marched past Tiflis' in 1264 as a campaign, not a holding; the Tokhtamysh page has a raid 'across the Caucasus into Shirvan' (1394) and no raid on Georgia. Georgia is cut out; the Terek-Caucasus frontier stays. Revised by fx-41 (window request R051): Khwarezm (647 of the region's 844 cells lie in this outline) is cut out. In 1385-1387 it is the Sufi dynasty's land under Horde suzerainty (ledger/16 vassal_start 1383), which the sufi-dynasty-of-khwarazm dossier draws (its ledger/6 vassal_start under the Horde 1383, ledger/10 dissolve to the Timurids 1388), and from 1388 the Timurids'; the outline would have kept it as direct Horde land to 1394. Khwarezm: Sufi dynasty page, re-read 2 Nov 2026 (fx-41): Suleiman Sufi 'in 1387 revolted in concert with the khan's invasion of Transoxiana', Timur 'immediately took action against Suleiman Shah, overrunning Khwarezm and crushing the rebellion' (no year; ruler list 'Sulayman (1380-1388)'), 'In the 15th century Khwarezm was usually controlled by the Timurids'; a Sufid in Timur's army 'rebelled in 1393/4, but was defeated and imprisoned'. No page returns it to the Horde.

The Khalkha page has the Khalkha khans ruling Outer Mongolia in the 17th century and Galdan's invasion of 1688, after which the Khalkha lose their independence; no page opened gives the 1691 submission. The shape is a Mongol-khanate shape of the Northern Yuan line (to 1635, the mongol-khanate dossier) and then the Khalkha khanates; it should be re-attributed there and deleted from the Golden Horde.

ledger.note: 1294: the Jochid ulus appears as a separate state on Cliopatria's map when its Mongol Empire row ends in 1293. The page's own dates are older: infobox 'Established c. 1225 (Jochi's lands)', Batu from 1242 (infobox), with the page showing the ulus acting as its own state by 1262 ('Golden Horde-Ilkhanate war broke out'); the pre-1294 phase belongs to the mongol-empire dossier, which hands the land over in 1294. fx-13 (F308): Georgia is cut out of the founding shape (156 cells of modern Georgia in the Cliopatria outline); see the keyframe notes 1294-1326.

region.text: the Jochid ulus: the Kipchak steppe from the Danube to the Irtysh, the Volga and the Crimea, with Khwarazm and the Rus' lands as tributaries; without Georgia, south of the Caucasus

ledger.note: 1294: the Rus' princedoms pay tribute to Sarai. 'Batu installed Alexander as grand prince of Vladimir' (1252); a census in 1274-1275 covered 'all cities, including Smolensk and Vitebsk'; 1327 'Oz Beg backed Moscow as the leading Russian state'. The relation predates the dossier's first year; Cliopatria's Moscow row (1294-1546) is the drawn land.

region.text: the Moscow principality, tributary of Sarai

ledger.note: 1294: the grand principality of Vladimir is held by Sarai's appointment ('Batu installed Alexander as grand prince of Vladimir', 1252; 'Mikhail of Tver executed in Sarai', 22 November 1318).

region.text: the grand principality of Vladimir-Suzdal, whose grand princes are named by the khan

ledger.note: 1294: Galicia-Volhynia is a Horde tributary. 'Daniel of Galicia pledged allegiance to Batu' (1245); in 1259 'Boroldai's ultimatum' made Daniel 'pull down his city walls'. Cliopatria's Galicia-Volhynia row runs 1294-1351.

region.text: Galicia-Volhynia, whose princes paid allegiance to Batu from 1245

ledger.note: 1307: Toqta besieges Caffa. 'Toqta besieged Caffa' (1307); 'Caffa plundered' (1308). The Genoese colony in the Crimea; the Genoese had been given trade rights in Caffa and Azov in the 1267 peace.

region.text: Caffa (Feodosia), the Genoese trading colony in the south-east Crimea

ledger.note: 1308: Caffa is plundered and the siege ends. 'Caffa plundered' (1308); the page then records a Genoese trade treaty in 1339 and a failed Horde attempt to seize Caffa in 1344.

region.text: Caffa (Feodosia), the Genoese trading colony in the south-east Crimea

ledger.note: 1349: Galicia-Volhynia is lost to Poland and Hungary. 'Poland-Hungary occupied Galicia-Volhynia, ending Horde vassalage there.'

region.text: Galicia-Volhynia occupied by Poland and Hungary

ledger.note: 1356: Jani Beg takes Tabriz. 'Tabriz conquered' (1356, Golden Horde page); the Ilkhanate page puts 'Jani Beg of the Golden Horde took Tabriz for a year' in 1357 and calls it the end of the Ilkhanate remnant. Cliopatria does not draw Azerbaijan in the Golden Horde shape. Counterpart (reviewer ia-02-b): the Golden Horde page has Jani Beg conquer Tabriz, 'ending Chobanid rule there in 1356', and the Ilkhanate page calls it 'Chupanid-held Tabriz'; the Ilkhanate dossier ends in 1343.

region.text: Tabriz and the surrounding Azerbaijan

ledger.note: 1357: Azerbaijan is lost again. Golden Horde page: 'Following the assassination of Jani Beg, the Golden Horde quickly lost Azerbaijan to the Jalayir king Shaikh Uvais in 1357'; Berdi Beg was killed in the coup of Qulpa in 1359. fx-13 (F038): region widened from East Azarbaijan alone to East and West Azarbaijan, the 'Azerbaijan' of the page and of the jalayirid-sultanate dossier (its own gain is dated August 1358 there, so West Azarbaijan now passes here, one year earlier).

region.text: Iranian Azerbaijan around Tabriz (East and West Azarbaijan), as the jalayirid-sultanate dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1357: the Horde holds none of the rest of the Chobanid realm. chobanids.json ledger/4-5 (1357 loss and dissolve) hands this state the whole Cliopatria Chobanid realm (826 cells: Zanjan, Ardebil, Kordestan, Qazvin, Gilan, Van, Markazi, Hamadan and the Araxes and Mugan lands besides East and West Azarbaijan), but the Jani Beg page has only 'In the winter of 1356-1357, Jani Beg attacked the region of Azerbaijan in Iran', the conquest of Tabriz and a governor installed there; after the Jochid armies left the governor declared independence, the Muzaffarid ruler Mubariz al-Din Muhammad killed him and withdrew because he could not hold the city, and the Jalayirids annexed the region afterwards (page paraphrased; no year given). Golden Horde page: 'Jani Beg ... conquered Tabriz, ending Chobanid rule there in 1356'. Nothing opened has the Horde in Zanjan, Qazvin, Gilan or Kordestan. Without this loss the Horde kept 523 of those cells from 1357 to 1381, which showed as the 1363 and 1375 conflicts with the Jalayirids and the 523 cells removed by the 1381 keyframe snap (fx-13, F038). The land goes to nobody; the jalayirid-sultanate dossier's own gain of Iranian Azerbaijan (1358) is unchanged.

region.text: the Chobanid realm and the Tabriz district outside East and West Azarbaijan: the Horde's governor held Tabriz only, and it did not last

ledger.note: 1362: Lithuania takes Kiev and Podolia. 'The victory brought Kiev and a large part of present-day Ukraine ... under the control of the expanding Grand Duchy of Lithuania'; 'Podolia was entrusted to Aleksander, Yuri, Konstantin, and Fyodor'. The page dates the battle 'autumn 1362 or 1363' (the Mamai page says 1362). Cliopatria's Blue and White shapes of 1363 lack 1,817 cells that sit in Lithuania's 1363 shape.

region.text: Kiev and the Dnieper-Bug lands to Podolia

ledger.note: 1362: Moldavia breaks away. 'The Principality of Moldavia asserted their independence from the Golden Horde by supporting Lithuania in this battle.' The 1363 Blue and White shapes lack 390 cells that sit in Moldavia's 1363 shape.

region.text: the Moldavian lands between the Carpathians and the Dniester

ledger.note: 1363: the Great Troubles divide the Horde. The pages give no split date; they give 'the Blue Horde's period of anarchy (1359-1380)' (White Horde page) and Berdi Beg's death in August 1359 (Mamai page). 1363 is Cliopatria's first year of separate Blue and White shapes; Mamai had proclaimed his own khan in the Crimea in 1361.

region.text: the western wing: Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Pontic and Lower Volga steppe, under Mamai

ledger.note: 1363: the eastern wing, Orda's ulus, is drawn apart (Kazakh steppe, Syr Darya, Khwarazm). 'Formed around 1225, after the death of Jochi'; no page dates its separation from Sarai.

region.text: Orda's ulus: western Central Asia and south-western Siberia, seat at Sighnaq

ledger.note: 1380: Tokhtamysh reunites the wings. 'He united the Blue Horde with the White Horde and created the Golden Horde in 1380' (Blue Horde page); the Golden Horde infobox gives 1379 and the Mamai page has Arab Shah yield Sarai to Tokhtamysh in early 1380 and the White Horde page has him wrest the White Horde in 1378.

region.text: the White Horde, absorbed by Tokhtamysh

ledger.note: 1380: Mamai's western horde is absorbed. Blue Horde page: 'He united the Blue Horde with his own White Horde and created the Golden Horde in 1380'; Tokhtamysh page: 'When he reunified the Golden Horde in 1380-1381, Tokhtamysh promised to revitalize and stabilize it' and 'Mamai was defeated by Tokhtamysh on the Kalka river in the autumn of 1381'. Dated 1380 (it was 1381) because the blue-horde dossier ends in 1380 and passes its land to this state: on reading tools/compile_dossiers.py merge(), a merge dated 1381 finds the Blue Horde already dead, and the compiler then blanks this state's own cells in the region (6,551 of the Blue Horde's 6,934 cells, which is what the 1381 keyframe snap had to put back). Mamai's death at the end of 1380 or the beginning of 1381 and the peace with the Genoese of the Crimea in early 1381 are from the earlier note (Mamai page, not reopened in fx-13).

region.text: the Blue Horde (Mamai's lands), absorbed by Tokhtamysh

ledger.note: 1383: Khwarazm returns to the Horde. 'He restored Golden Horde authority over the Sufi Dynasty in Khwarazm' (1383).

region.text: Khwarazm under the Sufi dynasty (Urgench)

ledger.note: Spring 1387: war with Timur for Azerbaijan and the Caucasus. Tokhtamysh 'crossed the mountains in the spring of 1387' and attacked Timur, who was wintering near Karabakh; the earlier winter 1384-1385 campaign that took Tabriz by storm was against Jalayirid Azerbaijan, and Timur conquered Azerbaijan in 1386 (Tokhtamysh page). Shirvan was raided in 1394. Year corrected from 1385 by reviewer ia-02-b to match the page and this dossier's war (1387-1395).

region.text: Azerbaijan, Karabakh, Shirvan and the Terek-Caucasus frontier

ledger.note: 1388: Timur destroys Khwarazm's tie to the Horde. 'Winter 1387-1388: He overran Central Asia, and Timur razed Gurganj in 1388.' The page does not say Timur annexed Khwarazm; Cliopatria keeps it in the Golden Horde shape to 1401 and draws it as Timurid from 1402. (fx-41: the keyframes golden-horde_1385 and _1395 no longer hold Khwarezm, so the Horde draws none of it after this vassal_end.)

region.text: Khwarazm, razed at Gurganj by Timur

ledger.note: 1395: the Terek decides the Caucasus. 'The main battle took place on 15-16 April 1395', Timur then 'devastated the Volga cities from old Astrakhan to Sarai' (winter 1395-1396). Cliopatria's 1395 shape loses 623 cells on its southern edge, 614 of them inside the Timurid Empire's 1395 shape; the region given is the Transcaucasian and North Caucasian part.

region.text: the Golden Horde's southern reach in the Caucasus that Cliopatria hands to Timur in 1395

ledger.note: 1395: the Tokhtamysh-Timur war ends at the Terek. 'The main battle took place on 15-16 April 1395'; the earlier rout at Kondurcha was on 18 June 1391.

region.text: Azerbaijan, Karabakh, Shirvan and the Terek-Caucasus frontier

ledger.note: 1402: the eastern steppe leaves the Golden Horde on Cliopatria's map. Page silent on 1402: the White Horde page has 'Kuruichik appointed head of the White Horde by Tamerlane' after 1395-1396; the Edigu page has Edigu 'a sovereign ruler of a large area stretching between the Volga and Ural' by 1396 and Tokhtamysh in Siberia 'in 1400'; Cliopatria draws no state on the Kazakh steppe until the Khanate of Sibir (1429). Counterpart is 'nobody' because no Cliopatria shape covers the land (the Orda ulus under Kuruichik and Edigu's Manghit ulus are the real holders).

region.text: the Kazakh steppe east of the Ural, Khwarazm and the Siberian margin that the 1402 shape drops

ledger.note: 1405: Edigu takes Khwarazm. 'Timur died the same year, after which Edigu's authority grew in Mangyshlak and south of the Aral Sea. Edigu also took Khwarezm, which he held until 1412.' Edigu ruled behind the Golden Horde's khans (commander-in-chief from 1397).

region.text: Khwarazm, held by Edigu until 1412

ledger.note: 1412: Khwarazm is lost. The page says Edigu took Khwarezm 'which he held until 1412'; it then has him seeking refuge there after losing 'Astrakhan, Bolghar, Crimea, and Sarai' by 1412-1413 until 'Shah Rukh expelled him from Khwarazm' (undated).

region.text: Khwarazm, from which Shah Rukh expelled Edigu

ledger.note: 1438: Kazan breaks away. 'Ulugh Muhammad was driven out in 1438 and founded the Khanate of Kazan.' Cliopatria's Kazan row and the 1440 Golden Horde shape (450 cells fewer) begin in 1440.

region.text: the Middle Volga: Kazan and Bolghar

ledger.note: August 1449: Crimea throws off Sarai. The Crimean Khanate 'had kicked out authority from Sarai in August 1449.' Cliopatria's Crimean Khanate starts 1450 and takes 814 cells of the 1440 Golden Horde shape.

region.text: the Crimean peninsula and the steppe north of it that Cliopatria gives the Crimean Khanate in 1450

ledger.note: 1450: the steppe east of the Volga passes to the Nogai Horde on Cliopatria's map (1,553 cells). Page silent on a date: the Edigu page makes Edigu 'regarded as founder of the Manghit ulus, later the Nogai Horde', and the Great Horde page says the breakup 'fractured into the separate states of the Nogai Khanate, the Kazan Khanate' after Edigu's death in 1419.

region.text: the Volga-Ural steppe east of the Volga that Cliopatria gives to the Nogai Horde in 1450

ledger.note: 1453: small border losses on the Oka and Moksha. Page silent: the Great Horde page names the Kasimov Khanate as 'a later separate state' without a date; 167 cells go to Cliopatria's Qasim Khanate (94) and Ryazan (72).

region.text: the Mokshan-Oka frontier land that Cliopatria gives to the Qasim Khanate in 1453

ledger.note: 1453: 72 cells of the same step pass to Ryazan. Page silent on the date.

region.text: the frontier land that Cliopatria gives to Ryazan in 1453

ledger.note: 1468: Astrakhan breaks away. 'Mahmud broke away to found the Astrakhan Khanate after 1465' (Mahmud was 'usurped by his brother Ahmed Khan bin Kucuk in 1465'); Cliopatria's Astrakhan row starts 1468 and takes 549 cells of the Golden Horde shape.

region.text: the Lower Volga that Cliopatria gives to the Astrakhan Khanate in 1468

ledger.note: 1480: the Ugra stand ends Moscow's vassalage. Ahmed's campaign against Moscow ('Great Stand on the Ugra River: 1480') ended when he 'judged the conditions unfavorable and retreated', and the incident 'formally ended the "Tatar yoke" over Russia' (Great Horde page, which also says 'By the 1470s, Muscovy had stopped paying tribute to Sarai'). Ahmed was killed by Ibak on 6 January 1481. Confidence raised from 1 by reviewer ia-02-b.

region.text: Moscow, no longer tributary after the Ugra

ledger.note: 1480: Vladimir-Suzdal (by then ruled from Moscow) leaves the vassal tint with Moscow: the Ugra stand 'formally ended the "Tatar yoke" over Russia' (Great Horde page). Confidence raised from 1 by reviewer ia-02-b.

region.text: Vladimir-Suzdal, merged into Moscow's lands

ledger.note: June 1502: the Golden Horde ends. 'Sack of Sarai by the Crimean Khanate: 10 June 1502' and 'Battle of Samara River ending the Great Horde: 28 June 1502'; 'the Crimean Khanate subjugated what remained of the Great Horde'; 'Ahmed's descendants occupying the throne of Astrakhan in 1502'. Cliopatria's last shape ends 1501.

region.text: the Great Horde's rump around Sarai

wars.name: Golden Horde invasions of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: No border change: Oz Beg invades Azerbaijan in 1318/1319, 1324 and 1335; Abu Said dies on the way to meet the last, in Karabakh, in 1335.
wars.note: The Golden Horde page lists '1318, 1324, 1335: Invasions of the Ilkhanate'; the Abu Said page dates Oz Beg's invasion to 1319 and the last to 1335.

wars.name: Horde-Genoese conflict at Caffa
wars.outcome: Toqta besieges Caffa in 1307 and plunders it in 1308; Jani Beg's attempt to seize it fails in 1344 and the Black Death is reported in the siege of 1346. The Genoese keep the colony.
wars.note: Dates as the Golden Horde page lists them: 1307 siege, 1308 plundered, 1344 failed attempt, 1346 plague at the siege.

wars.name: Conquest of Azerbaijan by Jani Beg
wars.outcome: Tabriz is taken in 1356 and Azerbaijan is lost to Shaikh Uvais in 1357.
wars.note: The Ilkhanate page dates Jani Beg's capture of Tabriz to 1357 and says it lasted a year.

wars.name: Battle of Blue Waters

zones.text: Kiev, Podolia and the Moldavian lands

wars.outcome: Lithuanian victory: Kiev and a large part of present-day Ukraine pass to Lithuania, Moldavia asserts independence.
wars.note: The page dates the battle 'autumn 1362 or 1363'; the Mamai page says 1362.

wars.name: Great Troubles

zones.text: Sarai and the Lower Volga, the seat that changed hands among the khans of Mamai and Urus

wars.outcome: Succession war after Berdi Beg's murder (August 1359); the Horde divides into Mamai's western and Orda's eastern wings until Tokhtamysh takes Sarai in 1380.
wars.note: The Mamai page lists the khans seated at Sarai year by year, from Abdallah (installed 1362) and Murad (1362-1363) to Qaghan Beg (1375) and Arab Shah (1377 to early 1380).

wars.name: Tokhtamysh's sack of Moscow
wars.outcome: Moscow is besieged on 23 August 1382 and stormed three days later; tribute is restored. No land changes.

wars.name: Tokhtamysh-Timur war

zones.text: Azerbaijan, Karabakh, Shirvan and the Terek frontier

wars.outcome: Timur routs Tokhtamysh at Kondurcha (18 June 1391) and on the Terek (15-16 April 1395) and devastates the Volga cities in the winter of 1395-96; the Golden Horde loses its southern reach.

wars.name: Battle of the Vorskla River

zones.text: the steppe between the Dnieper and the Don

wars.outcome: On 12 August 1399 Edigu and Timur-Qutlugh defeat Tokhtamysh and Vytautas of Lithuania; Tokhtamysh flees to Siberia and Edigu 'united Jochi's lands under his rule' (Edigu page).
wars.note: Dated 'in 1399' on the Edigu page and 12 August 1399 on the Tokhtamysh page.

wars.name: Edigu's raid on Muscovy
wars.outcome: Edigu burns Nizhny Novgorod, Rostov and Serpukhov and besieges Moscow, which pays a ransom; no land changes.

wars.name: Break-up of the Golden Horde after Edigu

zones.text: the Middle Volga and the Crimea

wars.outcome: After Edigu's death in 1419 the Horde 'fractured into the separate states of the Nogai Khanate, the Kazan Khanate': Kazan 1438, Crimea August 1449.

wars.name: Great Stand on the Ugra River
wars.outcome: Ahmed's campaign against Moscow of 1480; he was killed by Ibak of Sibir on 6 January 1481. Ahmed retreated; the Great Horde page says the incident 'formally ended the "Tatar yoke" over Russia'.

wars.name: Great Horde-Crimean Khanate war

zones.text: the Great Horde's rump around Sarai

wars.outcome: 'From 1486 to 1491, a conflict raged between the Sarai-based Great Horde and the Crimean Khanate' (Casimir IV with the Great Horde, Ivan III with Mengli I Giray); on 10 June 1502 Mengli Giray sacks Sarai and on 28 June 1502 the Great Horde ends.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout, drawn approximate; no treaty or survey line appears on the pages opened. The Rus' princedoms are tributaries, not borders.

notes:
Start date: Cliopatria's row starts 1294 and the mongol-empire dossier hands the land over then; the Jochid ulus is older (infobox 'c. 1225', Batu 1242) and its pre-1294 years are not drawn separately (the Mongol Empire dossier lists uluses before 1294 as not written; an ia-02-x ulus dossier would need this dossier to start earlier). End date: June 1502 from the Great Horde page; Cliopatria stops at 1501.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO FIX. (1) Shapes 1547-1695 (15 shapes) are not the Golden Horde: they sit in Mongolia and are inside the Mongol Khanate shape of 1521; re-attribute to the Mongol khanates (mongol-khanate to 1635) and the Khalkha khanates (to 1691, no Cliopatria row), verdict wrong. (2) The Golden Horde has no shape in 1363-1384: Cliopatria draws the Great Troubles as the Blue and White Hordes; this dossier adds golden-horde_1381 (1381-1384, the union) and the blue-horde and white-horde dossiers end in 1380. (3) The Blue Horde row's Crimea-only shapes (1402-1449) are the peninsula, which this dossier takes back as union corrections on the 1385, 1395, 1402, 1431 and 1440 shapes. (4) The east of the realm (Kazakh steppe, Khwarazm, Siberian margin) has no Cliopatria state in 1402-1428; the 1402 loss is at confidence 1 with counterpart 'nobody'.

Page problems. The fetched Golden Horde page breaks off in 1359; everything later comes from the Blue Horde, White Horde, Tokhtamysh, Edigu, Great Horde, Mamai and Blue Waters pages. Discrepancies kept: Oz Beg's accession 1312/1313; the Blue Waters date 1362/1363; Tabriz 1356 (Golden Horde page) against 1357 (Ilkhanate page); Mamai's end at the Kalka 1380/1381; the union of the wings 1379 (infobox) / 1380 (Blue Horde page) / 1381 (first full year). The Great Horde page dates the Great Horde from the 1430s, not 1466, and gives June 1502 for the end; the Golden Horde infobox's 'Disintegrated into Great Horde: 1466' is therefore not used. The end of Moscow's vassalage in 1480 rests on the Great Horde page's 'formally ended the "Tatar yoke" over Russia' (confidence 2, raised by reviewer ia-02-b). The Cliopatria relation 'Allegiance of Golden Horde to Yuan 1294-1362' is not territory: the page has Toqta accepting the Yuan emperor's supremacy in 1304, relations reopening in 1326 and an annual 24,000 ding from Jochid appanages in China from 1339; it is not turned into a vassal event (the Golden Horde is the vassal, and the ledger's vassal events are for the state's own vassals). Smolensk, Nizhny Novgorod, Tver, Ryazan and Wallachia (independent from Hungary in 1330 with Oz Beg's backing) were tributaries or clients too but no page gives dates for the start and end, so no vassal pair is written.
